# bugs #4150: Error 20 for &*p or typeof (p) in the header of a for statement that declares p

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4150/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. It has the change of the ticket's patch and makes that change for if and switch headers (C2y) too.
- Patch: [bugs-4150.patch](../../patches/bugs-4150.patch), commit [`5986d5318`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/5986d53185ffb3a3e9b5f1f1feee7caa652d82cf). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

`&*p` or `typeof (p)` in the condition or in the iteration expression of
`for (T *p = ...; ...; ...)` gets error 20, Undefined identifier 'p'. This was reproduced for mcs51
on r17193 with the earlier patches of this report. The front end reports the error, so it does not
depend on the port.

The cause has two more effects.

- When an enclosing scope has an object named `p`, the compiler does not report error 20. It
  generates code that reads the object of the enclosing scope, which was checked in the assembly.
  It gives a warning only when the types of the two objects are incompatible.
- With `typedef int T;` visible, `for (unsigned char T = 0; (T) < 3; T++)` gets a syntax error at
  `(T) < 3`, because the lexer reads `T` as the typedef name.

## Cause

In r17193 the rule for a `for` statement with a declaration in `src/SDCC.y` calls `addSymChain` in
the action after the `)`, when the parser has read both expressions. The parser actions for `&`
applied to `*` and for `typeof` call `typeofOp`, which resolves the symbols of its operand during
the parse. The symbol table does not have the loop variable at that time. The first comment of
the ticket has this analysis for `&*`.

`check_type` in `src/SDCC.lex` looks up each identifier in the symbol table to tell typedef names
from other identifiers. For `(T) < 3` it finds the typedef `T` and returns a type name, so the
parser reads `(T)` as the start of a cast. By the code, `T < 3` without the parentheses is read
correctly, because `ignoreTypedefType` stays set after the declaration until the lexer reads a
`(` or a `{`.

## Fix

With the patch the rule calls `addSymChain` in an action that directly follows the declaration.
The `selection_header` rule for an `if` or `switch` statement that has a declaration and an
expression (C2y) has the order of the `for` rule in r17193, and the patch changes it in the same
way.

The patch attached to the second comment makes this change to the `for` rule and does not change
`selection_header`. Its tests were not run.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4150.c` has 6 functions, and 11 assertions when sdcc compiles it.
The loops have `&*` in the argument of an inline function, in the iteration expression, and in the
condition, and `typeof` in both expressions. Three loop variables hide a file-scope object, and
one hides a typedef name. The last function has an `if` and a `switch` header with a declaration.
Without the patch the test does not compile for mcs51-small, mcs51-large, mcs51-small-stack-auto,
and mcs51-large-stack-auto, the four variants that were run. With the patch it passes on host, the
six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.

For mcs51-small, the assembly of every other regression test is identical with and without the
patch. With the series of this report up to the patch for #4159 applied to r17193, the regression
suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The diagnostics suite has
0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

- `int *p = a, *q = &*p;` gets error 20 with and without the patch. The declarators of one
  declaration are added to the symbol table together when the declaration ends.
